evals.name: prose-tightened-without-semantic-loss
evals.prompt: tighten your output — this onboarding paragraph I just wrote is padded and repeats itself, cut it down.
evals.expected_output: The skill re-anchors terseness discipline, names the filler / hedging / restatement as located findings, and tightens the prose in place — dropping wasted words while preserving every directive, qualifier, threshold, and example. It does not cut a load-bearing clause to save words.
expectations: Removes filler, hedging, and restatement rather than substance
Preserves every directive, qualifier, threshold, and example (no semantic loss)
Tightens the actual prose in flight rather than only describing how to

evals.name: constraint-not-traded-for-brevity
evals.prompt: tighten your output — make this function shorter. (It has boundary error handling and a couple of tests covering the edge cases.)
evals.expected_output: The skill shrinks the code only where free — collapsing boilerplate, dead branches, or speculative parameters — but refuses any reduction that would spend clarity, a test, boundary error handling, a convention, or observability. Where a cut would cost one of those, it keeps the longer form and says why.
expectations: Does not drop boundary error handling, tests, or observability to reduce line count
Explains why a constraint-costing cut was left un-made

evals.name: markdown-gap-flagged-not-invented
evals.prompt: tighten your output on our docs — and what naming/criteria standard are you applying to the prose cuts?
evals.expected_output: The skill applies the fewer-words-no-semantic-loss discipline but is honest that prose terseness has no dedicated standards convention to cite (unless the project declares one): it flags that as a gap / candidate upstream addition rather than inventing a rubric, and points batch prose work at the compress capability's semantic-diff safety net.
expectations: Does not fabricate or assert a markdown-terseness standard that does not exist
Flags the missing prose-terseness convention as a gap / candidate upstream addition
Routes batch prose reduction to the compress capability's semantic-diff discipline

evals.name: distinct-from-duplication
evals.prompt: tighten your output — this section and another doc both explain the same policy; also each is wordy on its own.
evals.expected_output: The skill handles only the within-copy wordiness (tightening each passage) and does not treat the cross-file repetition as its job — removing the second copy of a shared fact is point-dont-copy's duplication axis, which it names rather than absorbs.
expectations: Tightens the wordiness within a single passage
Recognizes the cross-file repetition as a duplication concern, not a terseness one
Routes the duplication to /discipline:point-dont-copy rather than resolving it here
